topic: The Architecture of Thought: Understanding Neural Networks

sections.title: The Biological Inspiration
lecture_lines: Neural networks are inspired by the human brain.
Interconnected neurons process information to make decisions.
Computers mimic this structure to recognize complex patterns.
animations: Show a biological neuron schematic (#ADD8E6) morphing into a digital node (#90EE90) to represent biomimicry.
Animate signals pulsing through interconnected nodes as the network processes data.
The output node glows and displays the label 'Pattern Recognized' in bright gold (#FFD700).

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Math of a Single Decision
lecture_lines: A single decision starts with a simple linear equation.
Weights adjust importance, while bias sets the threshold.
This mathematical line separates data into distinct categories.
animations: Display the linear equation y = wx + b in the center of the screen (#FFFFFF).
Label 'w' as 'Weight' (#FFD700) and 'b' as 'Bias' (#FF69B4) with emphasis flashes.
Draw a coordinate plane with a line (#00FFFF) separating two groups of data points.

sections.title: The Anatomy of a Neuron
lecture_lines: An artificial neuron receives multiple input signals.
Each input is multiplied by its unique weight.
The weighted inputs are summed with a bias value.
An activation function decides the final output strength.
This process determines if a signal passes forward.
animations: Visualize a neuron circle (#FFFFFF) with multiple incoming arrows for inputs (x1, x2, x3).
Display 'w1x1', 'w2x2', and 'w3x3' labels next to the arrows, highlighting them in yellow (#FFFF00).
Display the summation formula Σ(wx) + b inside the neuron, which pulses with light.
Animate a ReLU activation graph (#00FF00) appearing over the sum to transform the value.
A final signal pulse exits the neuron, its brightness reflecting the output value.

sections.title: Layered Architecture: Input, Hidden, and Output
lecture_lines: Neurons are organized into a tiered assembly line.
The input layer receives the raw digital data.
Hidden layers extract increasingly abstract features.
Each layer builds upon the findings of the previous.
Finally, the output layer delivers the network's prediction.
animations: Show three distinct layers of nodes: Input (#ADD8E6), Hidden (#98FB98), and Output (#FFA07A).
Input layer nodes flash to represent raw pixel data from a letter 'B'.
Hidden layer nodes highlight to show feature extraction of lines and circles.
Connections between layers glow as information propagates through the tiered structure.
The specific 'B' output node scales up and turns gold (#FFD700) to indicate prediction.

sections.title: The Mathematics of Forward Propagation
lecture_lines: Data flows forward through a series of matrix multiplications.
Input vectors are transformed by matrices of weights.
This creates a giant, complex mathematical function.
Every connection contributes to the final result.
Mathematical precision enables the network to 'think'.
animations: Display an input vector X and a weight matrix W in mathematical notation (#FFFFFF).
Animate the dot product by highlighting row-column multiplication in sync.
The camera zooms out to show multiple layers of matrices cascading.
Highlight all connections in the network simultaneously with a soft glow (#ADD8E6).
The final vector output flows into a 'Decision' node [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/decision.svg] that glows gold (#FFD700).

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Impact
lecture_lines: Networks learn by adjusting weights to minimize errors.
This technology powers self-driving cars and medical diagnoses.
Mathematical architecture transforms raw data into intelligent action.
animations: Display the full network with weights on connections changing color (#FF4500) to show learning.
Show labels 'Pedestrian' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pedestrian.svg] and 'Mailbox' being correctly identified by the output layer.
Fade in the summary text 'Mathematical Precision' at the bottom of the screen.
